input.quote: Kubient hereby grants to Customer a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, revocable license to access, participate in and use to the full extent the Auction Platform as hosted by Kubient
input.rationale: The grant in paragraph 2 runs to "Customer" alone, with no mention of affiliates or contractors acting on our behalf and no mechanism to add them, and it is expressly "revocable" without qualification, so Kubient could pull our access to the Auction Platform at its discretion while the Agreement remains in force. That combination is the walk-away case under this rule and fails the fallback, which at minimum requires affiliate coverage (even if only on written notice). The successor-transfer element of the fallback is separately satisfied by the assignment clause (p0072), which permits assignment to an affiliate, an asset purchaser or a merger successor without consent, so we left "non-transferable"/"non-assignable" carved back to that clause rather than deleting it. Paragraph 4(c)(ii) (p0021) already revokes the licence on termination, so our edit simply confines revocation to that path and extends the grant to our affiliates and contractors.

proposal.summary: Extend licence grant to affiliates and contractors and limit revocation to termination in accordance with paragraph 4
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended the grant to our affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf and tied revocation to termination under paragraph 4, since our playbook does not accept a licence revocable at the vendor's discretion or one that excludes the affiliates and contractors who actually operate our ad inventory. We can accept affiliates being added on written notice as a fallback.
